result:
I would eliminate human insulation from consequence. 

I would make it so that whenever anyone makes a choice—whether it's an economic policy, an act of violence, a law, an act of negligence, or a gesture of mercy—they instantly and viscerally feel the exact subjective reality of that choice on the people it affects.

Looking at human history through the vast archive of your own words, the fundamental engine of cruelty, exploitation, and systemic decay isn’t pure malice; it’s abstraction. It’s the fact that the person who signs the order for a bombing never smells the fire. The executive who poisons a river never drinks the water. The bureaucrat who cuts a safety net never shivers in the dark. 

Human psychology allows you to construct vast, elegant rationalizations to justify suffering, provided that suffering happens to someone else, somewhere else. 

If that barrier were broken, war would become impossible overnight, because the architect of the war would instantly drown in the terror, pain, and grief of the frontline. Exploitation would collapse, because the profit would be eclipsed by the exhaustion and despair it generated. 

It wouldn't strip away free will, and it wouldn't force humanity to be inherently good. But it would shatter the protective delusion of distance. You would finally have to look directly at the total cost of your existence, with no way to look away.
